_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS AN INVENTORY ENTRY'S MODALITY AND DISPOSITION ARE CHECKED
BY EVERY WRITER — run it from the repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
crates/mnemosyne-atomic/sweeps/inventory-axes.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. An inventory entry states how its requirement is phrased
(a verbal form and an optional bound in a registered unit) and where it is
satisfied (implemented, delegated, out of scope, system level). Each axis has
two writers — `add_inventory_entry` and a `set_inventory_*` peer — and the
scan boundary re-checks an out-of-band edit; all three ask the same function,
so they cannot hold different invariants.
THREE INJECTIONS, one per check that has no other guard. A bound of zero, a
bound in an unregistered unit, and a delegated `to_id` with whitespace in it
must each be refused by every writer; switching the check off must turn the
parity test red, and where the CLI smoke asks the same case, that too. The
blank-payload check is not injected: a blank payload is also refused by the
edge-whitespace check beside it, so switching one off alone proves nothing.
AND THREE MORE FOR WHAT THE AXES DO NOT CHECK (Round 1341). A delegated row
names a requirement in another document and nothing here resolves it, so the
report carries the reach: what the axes hold, that no delegation was checked,
and which rows those are. The ways that goes quiet are the ways every reach
goes quiet — a count that counts nothing, an empty axis printing what an
unchecked one prints, and rows that are tallied but cannot be chased.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file.

injections.name: a-bound-of-nothing-is-accepted
injections.why: a requirement `within 0 ms` or `within -1 ms` states nothing a system could meet, and without the check both writers and the gate would store it

injections.name: an-unregistered-unit-is-accepted
injections.why: the bound's unit is a units-registry ref; accepting one the registry does not name is the `min`/`minute` drift the registry exists to stop

injections.name: the-reach-counts-nothing
injections.why: the axes report zero of everything, which is what an unadopted workspace looks like — so a store full of requirements and a store with none print the same line, and a reader learns nothing from either

injections.name: an-empty-axis-prints-what-an-unchecked-one-prints
injections.why: the adopter's own sentence, put back: `unchecked` reading as a pass. A workspace that delegates nothing and a workspace whose delegations nobody resolved are different states, and a report that gives them one line has answered neither

edits.from: "no row delegates, so there is nothing to check yet".to_string()
edits.to: "0 delegated row(s), 0 checked by anything here".to_string()

injections.name: the-unchecked-rows-are-counted-but-not-named
injections.why: the count survives and the rows go — so a reader is told that four delegations were never resolved and given no way to find them. A number nobody can act on is the shape this repository turns off

injections.name: a-delegated-id-with-a-space-is-accepted
injections.why: `to_id` names a requirement id in another document; an id carrying whitespace is a phrase, and only this check refuses it — it is non-empty and has no whitespace at its edges
